title: Mira Murati's AI Startup Releases First Model in Bid to Loosen AI Giants' Grip
summary: Thinking Machines Lab, the AI startup led by former OpenAI CTO Mira Murati, released its first model, betting that more customizable AI systems can chip away at the dominance of frontier labs like OpenAI and Anthropic. The launch marks the company's first public product since it was founded and raised a large funding round to compete in the foundation-model race.

title: AT&T and Verizon Look Beyond the Family Plan
summary: AT&T and Verizon are rolling out new wireless service options designed to move beyond the traditional multiline family plan, aiming to capture long-term customers through more flexible offerings. The shift reflects carriers' efforts to differentiate in a wireless market where the family-plan model has become commoditized.

title: Meta Workers Accuse It of Using AI to Conduct Discriminatory Layoffs
summary: A lawsuit filed against Meta alleges the company used AI tools to help conduct layoffs that disproportionately targeted employees with disabilities and those on medical or parental leave. The suit adds to a growing set of legal challenges over employers' use of AI in workforce-reduction decisions.

title: U.A.E. Rewarded With Coveted AI Chips for Supporting U.S. War in Iran
summary: The United Arab Emirates has secured expanded access to advanced U.S. AI chips after backing American military action in Iran, with its flagship AI firm now able to freely purchase the hardware. The arrangement is tied to the UAE firm's plan to restructure as a U.S. company, underscoring how chip export policy is increasingly linked to geopolitical alignment.

title: IBM Loses $69 Billion of Market Value in One Day in Latest AI-Fueled Selloff
summary: IBM shares plunged 25% after preliminary second-quarter results showed weakness in its software and infrastructure business, as customers redirected spending toward AI infrastructure such as memory chips instead of traditional enterprise IT. The one-day, $69 billion market-value loss illustrated a widening divide between companies benefiting directly from AI infrastructure buildout, such as chip-equipment maker ASML, which raised its full-year guidance the same day, and legacy technology vendors being squeezed by the shift.

title: China's DeepSeek Prepares to List Shares in Shanghai Next Year
summary: Chinese AI developer DeepSeek is preparing to list its shares in Shanghai next year as it seeks additional funding to sustain costly research in its race against Anthropic and other U.S. AI labs. The Information separately reported DeepSeek's annualized revenue is nearing $500 million, a figure the company is citing to support its fundraising and IPO plans.

title: White House Launches Platform to Share AI Cyber Threats, Fixes
summary: The White House launched Gold Eagle, a clearinghouse joining federal agencies, AI developers and critical-infrastructure companies to coordinate discovery and patching of software vulnerabilities identified by AI systems. Built with Carnegie Mellon's Software Engineering Institute, the platform is a joint effort across Treasury, the Department of Homeland Security and the Pentagon, and has already begun processing vulnerability reports.

title: Microsoft's New Security Chief Replaces Top Execs to Force an AI Overhaul
summary: Microsoft's new security chief has replaced several top executives as part of an effort to overhaul the company's security business in response to AI-powered hacking threats. The leadership shakeup follows the executive's appointment earlier this year to lead Microsoft's security unit.

title: Cursor Is Reinventing Itself as SpaceX Deal Looms
summary: Coding startup Cursor is restructuring its business as it heads toward a planned $60 billion acquisition by SpaceX, with CEO Michael Truell outlining a major transformation to staff. The deal, expected to close roughly 30 days after SpaceX's IPO, would rank among the largest acquisitions of a venture-backed startup in history.

title: Amazon Gives Electrovaya a Jolt
summary: Ontario-based battery maker Electrovaya announced a commercial agreement with Amazon covering deployment of its Infinity lithium-ion battery technology in material handling operations, with potential expansion into robotics and energy storage. Amazon received warrants for up to roughly 21% of Electrovaya's shares, vesting as purchases under the deal reach $280 million, and the stock jumped nearly 50% on the news.

title: The Small Team in Montreal Trying to Save the World From AI
summary: LawZero, the Montreal nonprofit founded by AI pioneer Yoshua Bengio to build safer alternatives to commercial AI systems, is launching a fundraising campaign to grow its team past 200 staff after raising an initial $30 million from donors and winning support from the Gates Foundation. The federal government has signed a letter of intent to back LawZero, whose 'Scientist AI' approach aims to be explanatory and epistemically honest rather than pursuing autonomous, goal-driven systems.

title: BCG's Four CIO Pillars for Scaling Agentic AI
summary: Boston Consulting Group outlined four pillars for CIOs scaling agentic AI: optimizing existing technology, reshaping business functions, inventing new business opportunities, and reimagining entire organizations. BCG found that success with agentic AI is roughly 70% dependent on people and change management rather than algorithms, that only about 5% of companies are currently 'agent-first,' and that leading enterprises are cutting costs 15-20% across functions through graduated-autonomy deployment models.

title: Nokia Asserts AI-RAN Leadership
summary: Nokia launched a new AI-RAN platform aimed at boosting mobile network capacity and efficiency, built on an AI-native network architecture and leveraging Nvidia's accelerated computing technology. The move is part of a broader reorganization at Nokia around AI-driven network and data-center opportunities.

title: New York Puts Mega Data Centres on Ice
summary: New York became the first U.S. state to halt construction of large new data centers, imposing a one-year moratorium amid concerns over power demand and grid capacity. The pause highlights growing friction between AI-driven data-center growth and local energy infrastructure constraints.

title: TSMC Plans Another $100 Billion U.S. Investment as AI Demand Surges
summary: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. said it will invest another $100 billion in Arizona chipmaking and advanced-packaging capacity, bringing its committed U.S. investment to roughly $165 billion, after posting second-quarter revenue of about $39.6 billion (up 36% year-over-year) and raising its 2026 capital-spending forecast to $60-64 billion. CEO C.C. Wei said AI chip demand from cloud providers continues to outstrip supply, though AI-linked stocks broadly failed to rally on the results as investors questioned whether hyperscaler capital spending will pay off.

title: The AI Backlash Has Tech Executives Fearing for Their Lives
summary: Violent threats against AI companies and their executives have surged, prompting some tech leaders to travel with armed guards or avoid discussing AI publicly. Incidents include an April break-in at Anthropic's San Francisco lobby in which an intruder left a written death threat naming a senior executive, five days after an attempted firebombing of OpenAI CEO Sam Altman's home. Threat-monitoring firm Liferaft found digital threats against AI executives and data centers grew sevenfold between late February and May.

title: Thirst for AI Pushes Cyber M&A Toward a Record Year
summary: Cybersecurity M&A hit a record 219 deals worth $9.1 billion in the first half of 2026, driven partly by demand for tools that defend AI agents and large-language-model data. June produced the year's first billion-dollar-plus deal, Accenture's $4.175 billion purchase of Dragos, NetRise and runZero, following Alphabet's $32 billion Wiz acquisition in March, the largest pure-play cybersecurity deal on record.

title: Hackers Claim Data Theft From India's Largest Nuclear Plant
summary: A ransomware group calling itself World Leaks posted roughly 19,000 files, totaling 14.3 gigabytes, allegedly from India's Kudankulam Nuclear Power Plant, including engineering blueprints, supplier records and inspection reports tied to two reactor units. Contractor Reliance Group confirmed a partial breach of data hosted with a third-party provider, while India's Nuclear Power Corporation said no nuclear-safety or security systems were affected; the plant was previously linked to a 2019 North Korean malware incident.

title: Nobody Is Immune From the GPU Crunch
summary: Startups are increasingly shifting workloads away from Amazon Web Services and other established cloud providers toward smaller challengers such as Nebius as a shortage of AI computing capacity intensifies. The Information separately reported that Microsoft and other large cloud providers are hoarding GPUs, creating a bottleneck that is squeezing AI startups' access to compute just as demand for training and inference capacity keeps climbing.

title: Cursor Is Developing an AI Agent to Compete With Claude Cowork
summary: Cursor, the AI coding startup, is building a general-purpose AI agent intended to compete with Anthropic's Claude Cowork, part of a broader push to expand beyond coding tools. The company's CEO told staff in a May all-hands meeting that Cursor aims to become a top-tier AI model developer in its own right, a push that coincides with reported takeover interest from SpaceX valuing the company near $60 billion.

title: Microsoft Memo Details AI App Overhaul to 'Earn the Right to Exist'
summary: An internal Microsoft memo outlines plans to merge the company's consumer and enterprise Copilot applications and cut underused features, as executives push AI products to prove their value to users. The overhaul reflects pressure inside Microsoft to consolidate its sprawling AI product lineup amid intensifying competition for enterprise AI spending.

title: Stripe, Advent Made Joint Offer to Buy PayPal
summary: Stripe and private-equity firm Advent International submitted an unsolicited joint offer to acquire PayPal for $60.50 a share, valuing the payments company at more than $53 billion, a roughly 28% premium to its prior closing price. The bid includes about $50 billion in committed financing, with PayPal's board expected to review the offer as soon as July 20.

title: Citi Sees Canada Heating Up in Global Capital Shift
summary: Citi Canada is expanding its local workforce by about 1,000 additional roles after already growing headcount by some 1,500 employees in recent years, according to CEO Raymond Gatcliffe, who cited the country's shifting role in trade, resources and defence. The bank purchased its Mississauga office campus in June after leasing the site since 2007; the location now employs about 3,500 people, roughly 75-80% of them in technology roles.

title: EU Hands SFR Carve-Up Antitrust Review to France
summary: The European Commission referred its review of Iliad's portion of the three-way breakup of Altice France's SFR to France's Autorite de la concurrence, part of a EUR20.35 billion carve-up in which Bouygues Telecom, Iliad and Orange are splitting SFR's assets and subscribers. The French regulator's review is expected to take at least 18 months given the deal would cut France's mobile operators from four to three, a structure EU regulators have historically resisted.

title: TikTok in Ofcom Crosshairs Over Child Safety
summary: UK regulator Ofcom opened a formal investigation into TikTok on July 16 over concerns that its age-inference methods are failing to reliably identify child users, potentially exposing them to harmful content under the Online Safety Act. The probe, expected to take at least three months with an update due in October, could result in fines of up to £18 million or 10% of TikTok's global revenue if breaches are found.

title: Meet the Companies Shelling Out for Top AI Models
summary: Some companies are paying steep and rising premiums for more powerful 'frontier' AI models rather than switching to cheaper alternatives, according to The Wall Street Journal. The report examines which firms are willing to absorb higher costs to access the most capable systems from leading AI labs.

title: SpaceX in Talks to Provide Computing Power for Pentagon's AI Push
summary: SpaceX is in talks to supply the Pentagon with data-center computing capacity worth billions of dollars to support the U.S. military's artificial intelligence initiatives, people familiar with the matter told The Wall Street Journal. The arrangement would extend SpaceX's role beyond satellite launches and communications into AI infrastructure for defense.

title: AI Is Becoming a Commodity, and That's a Problem for OpenAI and Anthropic
summary: As AI intelligence becomes cheaper and more commoditized, leading labs including OpenAI and Anthropic face pressure on the pricing power underpinning their business models, while lower-cost competitors stand to benefit. The shift raises questions about whether frontier labs can sustain the premiums that have justified their valuations.

title: China's Xi Touts Open-Source AI and Takes a Swipe at U.S. Dominance
summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping promoted open-source AI development and criticized U.S. dominance in the technology while courting developing countries at a Shanghai AI conference, as Beijing and Washington compete for global AI leadership. The Information separately covered the same conference, reporting Xi's call for 'open source, open collaboration.'

title: The Inside Story of IBM's Shocking Profit Warning
summary: IBM's recent profit warning followed a strategic bet on financial transparency that backfired, according to The Wall Street Journal's account of internal decisions at the company. The report examines whether CEO leadership can restore investor confidence after the warning rattled markets and erased billions in market value.

title: Startup OpenRouter Fields Multi-Billion-Dollar Takeover Interest
summary: OpenRouter, a startup that lets developers choose among hundreds of AI models through a single interface, has drawn significant investor and acquisition interest as its valuation has climbed toward $1.3 billion. The company recently closed a Series B round led by Google's CapitalG with participation from Nvidia's venture arm, reflecting the growing strategic value of AI model-routing infrastructure.

title: Moonshot AI's New Kimi K3 Challenges U.S. Frontier Models
summary: Chinese AI lab Moonshot AI unveiled its Kimi K3 model, reigniting debate over whether the performance gap between Chinese open-source models and U.S. frontier labs is narrowing. The release follows a string of increasingly capable open-source models from Moonshot, including earlier versions focused on coding and multimodal understanding.

title: Exclusive: Microsoft Preps Mythos-Like AI Bug Finder
summary: Microsoft is preparing to launch an AI-powered security product, internally codenamed Project Perception, that combines models from Anthropic, OpenAI and its own systems to detect and automatically fix software vulnerabilities. The tool, expected to debut as soon as this month, mirrors capabilities demonstrated by Anthropic's Mythos model and aims to capture a share of companies' growing cybersecurity spending.

title: Meta Plans To Hire Top AWS Executive
summary: Meta is set to hire Dave Brown, a senior Amazon Web Services executive who has spent nearly 19 years at the company, to help lead its AI data-center buildout. The move is part of Meta's push to expand Meta Compute, a cloud infrastructure effort that would put it in more direct competition with AWS, Microsoft Azure and Google Cloud.

title: Demand for Data Software Could Drive M&A Rebound
summary: The Information published a list of more than 160 enterprise software startups it considers potential acquisition targets this year, citing weak IPO markets and investor capital shifting toward AI as pressure points. Data-software companies in particular are seeing rising M&A interest as buyers look to fill gaps in AI-related product capabilities.

title: Verizon cuts corporate jobs, trims retail footprint
summary: Verizon will sell 274 company-owned retail stores and cut roughly 500 corporate jobs, affecting about 3,000 employees in total, as part of a restructuring under CEO Dan Schulman. The affected stores will shift to independent ownership rather than closing, continuing a cost-cutting drive that included a larger, 13,000-job reduction last year.

title: Ericsson recruited to UK defence list
summary: Ericsson has been selected as a supplier under the UK government's roughly £8 billion Tactical Communication Systems framework, covering private 5G, AI and drone technology for the armed forces through 2034. Rival vendor Nokia was not included on the framework, leaving Ericsson with a more direct route into UK military procurement.

title: Digital Equity Act to restart without race-based provisions
summary: A federal judge ruled that the U.S. Digital Equity Act's broadband grant programs can resume without the law's original race-based eligibility criteria, which were found unconstitutional. The ruling allows roughly $2.75 billion in broadband-adoption funding to move forward, minus provisions giving special consideration to racial or ethnic groups, while a $250 million tribal set-aside remains intact.

title: Companies want the AI productivity boost, but not the big bills
summary: Firms that previously encouraged unlimited employee use of AI tools are now reining in usage as costs mount, according to The Logic's Murad Hemmadi. The shift reflects growing scrutiny of AI spending among Canadian businesses even as they continue to pursue productivity gains from the technology.

title: From CLOs to ATMs, Wall Street Finds More Ways to Fund AI
summary: Wall Street is expanding beyond traditional debt to finance the AI data-center buildout, turning to collateralized loan obligations, asset-backed securities and other structured finance tools as capital needs scale into the trillions of dollars. The shift reflects growing appetite among banks and investors to package AI infrastructure debt into a wider range of instruments as funding needs outpace conventional lending capacity.

title: Cursor Is Reinventing Itself as SpaceX Deal Looms
summary: Cursor, the AI coding startup reportedly in talks to be acquired by SpaceX, is building a general-purpose AI agent meant to compete with tools like Anthropic's Claude, expanding beyond its core coding-assistant product. The push follows Cursor's move to begin leasing compute from SpaceX's AI unit and comes as the two companies work toward a jointly developed AI model.

title: AWS Is Overloaded, Cloud Startups Are Picking Up the Slack
summary: Amazon Web Services is struggling to meet demand for AI computing capacity, pushing some customers toward smaller cloud rivals; one startup, Arcee, committed to spend $8 million over three years with AWS but still could not secure enough Nvidia-powered servers to run its workloads. The capacity crunch reflects a broader GPU shortage across major cloud providers as AI compute demand continues to outstrip supply.

title: Microsoft's New Security Chief Replaces Top Execs to Force an AI Overhaul
summary: Microsoft, the world's largest seller of cybersecurity software, is overhauling that business to capitalize on corporate anxiety about AI-powered hacking, with security chief Hayete Gallot replacing top executives since taking over the unit in February. The restructuring is aimed at positioning Microsoft to capture rising enterprise spending on AI-related cyber defense.

title: What to Know About the Chinese AI Models Rattling U.S. Stocks
summary: The emergence of low-cost, high-performing Chinese AI models, such as Moonshot's Kimi K3, is raising fresh doubts about the durability of the U.S. AI investment boom and has contributed to volatility in American tech stocks. The article examines how these Chinese models compare with leading U.S. offerings and what their rise could mean for the competitive balance in AI development.

title: IBM CEO Arvind Krishna Has Nowhere to Hide From AI
summary: IBM's position in the current technology cycle has grown increasingly precarious as the company struggles to demonstrate it can capitalize on the AI boom the way rival tech firms have, putting pressure on CEO Arvind Krishna's strategy. The piece examines how IBM's legacy business model is being tested by the broader industry shift toward AI-native computing.

title: The Investors With a New Way to Win in Silicon Valley
summary: Venture-capital firms are adopting new tactics to gain access to the most sought-after AI startups amid a historic, once-in-a-lifetime IPO boom, rewriting long-standing conventions around deal structuring and founder access. The shift reflects intensifying competition among investors for stakes in a small number of dominant AI companies.

title: Pastors Using AI to Help Write Sermons Grapple With Where to Draw the Line
summary: A growing number of American pastors are using AI tools to help draft sermons, prompting debate within congregations over where assistance ends and authentic religious authorship begins. Critics argue the practice undermines the personal, spiritual nature of preaching, with one skeptic likening it to a betrayal of tradition. The piece examines how churches are informally setting boundaries around AI's role in religious writing.

title: Trump's AI Agenda Collides With Reality
summary: Nearly halfway into President Trump's second term, his light-touch AI deregulation agenda, launched via an executive order that rolled back Biden-era AI safety rules with adviser David Sacks, has been complicated by rising public concern. Fears about cybersecurity risks from frontier models such as Anthropic's Mythos, along with anxiety over AI's effects on jobs and electricity prices, have prompted hundreds of state, city, and county governments to pass AI-related bans and moratoriums, threatening the U.S. data center construction boom.

title: SAP-Oxford Economics: 2,600 leaders on AI ROI
summary: A joint SAP and Oxford Economics survey of 2,600 business leaders across 13 countries found that AI now supports 30% of tasks in the average business, up from 25% a year earlier. The average firm expects to spend $28 million on AI this year, projected to rise 45% within two years, while anticipated ROI is forecast to grow from $6.3 million (21%) this year to $15.9 million (38%) in two years; data quality, skills, and governance remain the top barriers to realizing that return.

title: Agentic AI's impact on the sales lifecycle
summary: A McKinsey report outlines how agentic AI is reshaping B2B sales and growth functions, identifying five priority "impact journeys" that place AI agents at the center of finding opportunities, choosing go-to-market models, designing offers, and setting prices. The report also details the operating-model shifts companies need to make to scale AI adoption across sales organizations and sustain the change.

title: The commercial AI sovereignty market
summary: Stanford's Institute for Human-Centered AI published a 20-page brief evaluating the emerging market for commercial "AI sovereignty" offerings, which let organizations or governments claim greater control over AI infrastructure and data. The brief finds that sovereignty is not a binary condition but a spectrum, and assesses how vendor offerings differ in design, marketing claims, and their actual effect on operational control and dependency reduction.

title: China's Top AI Event Delivers Message to the U.S.: We're Coming for You
summary: At the World Artificial Intelligence Conference in Shanghai, Chinese firms showcased AI progress that undercuts any lingering hope of a clear U.S. lead in the technology. Alibaba underscored the shift by previewing Qwen3.8-Max, a 2.4-trillion-parameter model it says trails only Anthropic's flagship system among frontier AI, sending Alibaba shares up as much as 5.4%.

title: The Massive Supply Deals Feeding the AI Frenzy Are No Sure Thing
summary: Long-term chip and memory supply agreements underpinning the AI buildout, including those touted by suppliers like SK Hynix, are less secure than markets assume, raising the risk that the current pace of AI infrastructure investment could be disrupted.

title: These AI-Native Companies Have Tiny Staffs and Fewer Bosses
summary: Startups built from the outset around AI tools are operating with far leaner headcounts and flatter management structures than earlier generations of technology companies, reshaping assumptions about how much staff a growing company needs.

title: Neo Emerges From Stealth With $100 Million to Secure Enterprise AI Agents
summary: Cybersecurity startup Neo, founded by former SentinelOne, Wiz and Palo Alto Networks executives, emerged from stealth with $100 million in funding, including a $75 million round led by Andreessen Horowitz and Bessemer Venture Partners. The company is building a control layer meant to govern AI agents and AI-enabled software across enterprise environments.

title: Coca-Cola Suspends U.S. Fairlife Production After Ransomware Attack
summary: Coca-Cola disclosed that its Fairlife dairy subsidiary detected unauthorized third-party access to its systems, including production systems, in a ransomware event that forced a temporary suspension of U.S. manufacturing. Fairlife, an estimated $4 billion brand, said Canadian production was unaffected and that product quality and safety were not compromised.

title: The Real Difference in the AI Era
summary: Bausch + Lomb CEO Brent Saunders has made AI training mandatory and tied it to employee pay, arguing the central risk of the AI era is not that AI replaces workers but that employees who don't adopt it will be replaced by those who do. The company partnered with Coursera to run an AI academy for roughly 8,000 employees.

title: Samsung Is the New Memory Chip Underdog—for Now
summary: A sell-off this month in memory chip stocks—Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron—has left the sector trading at a discount, giving investors a fresh entry point into a business that continues to benefit from AI-driven demand growth.

title: FCC Eyes Overhaul of USF Management and Oversight
summary: FCC Chairman Brendan Carr proposed a rulemaking seeking comment on how the Universal Service Fund is administered, including the role of the Universal Service Administrative Company, its board, and its operating costs. A full commission vote is expected August 6 and would mark the first structural review of USF administration since USAC was first selected.

title: TIM Takeover Bid Goes Live After Board Backing
summary: Italy's Poste Italiane launched its formal tender offer for Telecom Italia, a cash-and-share deal worth roughly €10.8 billion, after securing TIM board support. The offer requires regulatory approval, with Poste Italiane targeting completion by the end of 2026.

title: Meta in Early Talks to Lease AI Compute to Anthropic
summary: Meta is in preliminary talks to lease AI computing capacity to Anthropic in a deal reported to be worth about $10 billion, with Anthropic paying in monthly installments over two years. The talks are notable because Meta's Llama models compete directly with Anthropic's Claude, meaning Meta could become both a rival and a critical infrastructure supplier.

title: The Canadian Companies Trying to Break Palantir's Grip on Intelligence Software
summary: Canadian firms Anvil and Caseway are building intelligence and data-analysis software positioned to compete with Palantir, which holds significant Canadian government and law-enforcement contracts, including past deals with the Department of National Defence and the Ontario Provincial Police.
